title: unified-constraint-orchestrator-and-tokenizer-edgecase-shim
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We've accumulated several ad-hoc constraint backends (CFG, regex, token-mask) and a set of tokenizer edge-case hacks scattered through the streaming/compat layers. This PR introduces a unified 'constraint orchestrator' that composes multiple backends deterministically, plus a lightweight tokenizer-edgecase shim that normalizes token boundaries for constrained decoding and streaming deltas.

Goals: 1) Make backend composition explicit and configurable per-route so teams can pick grammar-first or regex-first strategies. 2) Remove brittle token-boundary heuristics from the streaming path and centralize them in a well-tested shim. 3) Ensure OpenAI-compat streaming events and function/tool-calling delta frames honor constraint decisions and do not expose partially matched token sequences.

Main changes:
 - New orchestrator that implements a pluggable priority resolver: backends register predicate/score and the orchestrator produces a single set of allowed token IDs each step. The resolver supports combinators (first-match, longest-match, intersection) and route-level overrides.
 - Tokenizer-edgecase shim that: folds subword boundary anchors into backend constraints, exposes an API to map boundary decisions back to original UTF-8 spans, and provides a fast-path for byte-aligned tokenizers.
 - Regex backend rewrite to maintain character-level anchors in addition to token-level constraints so mixed-mode regex+grammar constraints behave deterministically.
 - CFG backend update to expose partial-match states (for streaming) so we can emit stable progress events without leaking incomplete terminal tokens.
 - Streaming shim updates: framing logic now buffers until a safe commit boundary (based on orchestrator signals) before emitting a delta; this fixes cases where downstream tools saw function-call tokens split across frames.
 - OpenAI-compat adapter mapping: changed how 'delta' events are assembled so the external event stream sees only committed token deltas; added translation layer for function/tool calling events to preserve argument-level structured-output.
 - Route config additions: per-route 'constraint_strategy' and 'tokenizer_shim' toggles; default preserves current behavior.
 - Extensive unit + fuzz tests for tokenizer edgecases and end-to-end streaming with function calls.

Rollout: feature gated, default off in production; staged enablement for internal canaries and a dedicated perf canary cluster.

Backwards compatibility: Behavior is opt-in via route config. We include a compatibility shim that approximates previous heuristics when the new orchestrator is disabled.

Testing notes: initial CI run uncovered a race where the streaming buffer could block under backpressure; fixed by adding a non-blocking fallback and a bounded queue with emitting heuristics.

Linked Linear items: ENG-4210 implement constraint orchestrator, ENG-4301 streaming token boundary stability. Related: ties into perf work for batching (ENG-4122) and the OpenAI compat delta cleanup (ENG-3977).
